A learning scientist at the intersection

I study how learners engage with products, programs, and simulations — and translate that understanding into design that improves real outcomes.

I am a doctoral candidate in the Learning Design and Performance Technology Ed.D. program at Florida State University, with a foundation spanning education, counseling, and technology.

My work bridges simulation-based learning, program evaluation, and data-informed instructional design. From building clinical reasoning scenarios for nursing students to evaluating enterprise AI adoption across a university, I bring rigorous research methods to questions of how people actually learn and perform.

I care about the full arc — designing the experience, measuring whether it worked, and feeding the evidence back into better practice.

Selected work

Program Evaluation · AI Adoption

Copilot for M365 Pilot Evaluation

Florida State University ITS · Spring 2024

As an Instructional Technology Services intern, I evaluated whether faculty and staff found Microsoft Copilot for M365 to be an effective productivity tool. I analyzed pre- and post-assessment survey data from a 426-participant, five-month study, coded qualitative feedback into thematic patterns, and produced the executive summary that informed leadership’s licensing decision.

Findings surfaced across five themes — awareness, productivity, accuracy, support, and functionality — alongside concrete recommendations grounded in adult-learning theory.

Simulation · Clinical Education

Simulation-Based Learning Design

FSU College of Nursing · 2025–Present

As Simulation Learning Specialist, I design, implement, and evaluate simulation experiences that build clinical reasoning, procedural skill, and professional judgment. I author structured patient scenarios mapped to course- and program-level competencies for both formative and summative assessment.

Working alongside faculty, I integrate learning-science principles into pre-clinical and clinical curricula, facilitate reflective debriefing emphasizing metacognition and deliberate practice, and use learner-performance data to drive remediation and accreditation reporting.

Instructional Operations

Adjunct Faculty Onboarding System

FSU Simulation Center

I co-own onboarding for simulation adjunct faculty — from Canvas enrollment and required coursework to Teams orientation and grading proficiency across MedAffinity and Canvas. The structured checklist reduces ramp-up friction and ensures new faculty master prebriefs, debriefs, and student evaluation workflows before stepping into the sim center.

Instructional Design · Learning Theory

Social Cognitive Theory Infographic

Learning Design Artifact

A visual learning resource translating Albert Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory into an accessible, single-page reference. The piece breaks down human agency into its core constructs — intentionality, forethought, self-regulation, self-reflectiveness, and collective agency — and grounds each in a concrete educational application.

It demonstrates my ability to distill dense theoretical frameworks into clear, learner-centered instructional design that supports comprehension and retention.

Instructional infographic — Bandura’s constructs with an applied education example
UX Prototype · Digital Design

Clinical Learning Center Prototype

FSU College of Medicine

A digital UI prototype mapping the user interface for a Clinical Learning Center website. The wireframe defines the information architecture and user flows — from a landing page and introduction, through a “Become a Standardized Patient” registration form, to authenticated sections and a location finder.

The prototype shows how I move from learner and stakeholder needs to concrete interface design, planning navigation and content structure before development begins.

Digital prototype — landing page, registration, and authenticated sections with mapped flows
Research Communication · Data Analytics

The Future of Data Analytics

EME6356 · Graduate Coursework

A research-based presentation examining emerging trends in data analytics and their implications for medical education and healthcare. The deck synthesizes peer-reviewed literature to explore automated decision-making, data storage, and privacy, alongside how data-driven methods improve policy, patient outcomes, and innovation.

It reflects my strength in translating scholarly research into clear, actionable communication for professional audiences.

Graduate presentation — data analytics trends grounded in current healthcare literature
